findings: VERIFIED (authority): dispatch is bounded to the configured synthetic successor — advance() hardcodes Controller.submit with kind='synthetic_success'/backend='linux' at the pinned source, and both finish() and advance() re-derive the expected proposal from the root-owned installed config, failing closed (SYNTHETIC_PROPOSAL_CHANGED) on any drift. The model can only echo the configured successor id or decline (task_id null); select_next re-validation at dispatch time rejects everything else. Successors map to None in ingest()'s allowed set and the constructor rejects duplicates/cycles, so chains are bounded to one hop; FAILED predecessors get review tasks but never proposals; scheduled-report evidence cannot inject an execution_proposal and finish() no-ops without a matching completion_ingest row.

VERIFIED (recovery/idempotency): durable intent (immutable .selected-dispatch.json plus selected_dispatch row) precedes submission; Controller.register rejects changed bindings and deduplicates identical resubmission after a lost response, so the 3-attempt ceiling (then durable BLOCKED) cannot mint a second job identity. Pause is checked under admission.lock — the same lock control() takes — so pause cannot race a submission. Missing/changed evidence (absent receipts, tampered consoles, changed intent file) lands in blocks or reconciliation states, never re-execution, and one bad pair does not block the other.

VERIFIED (privacy): model packets carry hash-bound completion receipts (console_sha256 digests, never console bytes), and the model-authored selection text (selected_dispatch.binding) is excluded from status() and from the scheduled-report selected_work projection. No patient/scientific dispatch surface exists in this route and existing gates are not referenced or weakened.

SUGGESTION (fail-closed race in finish()): a declined selection is inserted as status='INTENT' and only afterwards updated to 'DECLINED' in separate autocommit statements without admission.lock; a concurrent advance() can observe the transient INTENT row. It cannot dispatch (select_next rejects task_id null) but it consumes durable attempts and can transiently mark the row BLOCKED before the DECLINED overwrite. Smallest fix: insert with the final status, or perform insert-and-decide in one transaction.

SUGGESTION (availability): sqlite3 exceptions escape every handler — ingest, advance, bookkeeping, and the tick phase wrapper catch only (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError, OSError). If the execution state DB is rebuilt and a configured job completes under a new attempt id, completion_ingest's UNIQUE(job) raises sqlite3.IntegrityError, which escapes both handlers and crashes every subsequent tick — a persistent fail-closed outage instead of a recorded completion_block. Smallest fix: add sqlite3.Error to the caught tuples or map IntegrityError to the reconciliation block.

SUGGESTION (artifact litter): ingest() binds the report day to datetime.now(utc) per attempt while enqueue_report/finalize write immutable report/task files and a QUEUED reviews row before the coordinator COMMIT; a crash inside the transaction plus a retry on a later UTC day permanently orphans the earlier report, its tasks/<id> directory, and an unclaimable review row. No authority leaks; derive the day from the verified completion event or document/collect orphans.

NOTE (as designed): finish() marks the wake and completion_ingest PROCESSED even when the first submission attempt fails; the pending/blocked dispatch stays visible via selected_dispatch in status() and scheduled reports, preserving operator visibility.

investigator_notes: Approval covers reviewed source, not hosted installation or activation.

The suggested UNIQUE(job) failure scenario is an inference: the existing prior-job check normally skips that insertion. General SQLite errors were nevertheless not caught; follow-up records those failures and explicitly detects changed completion identity.
Follow-up stores declines in their final state and retains first-observation evidence across report retries. No prior scientific approval or completed model receipt is relabeled.
